attempts.summary: On node1 (Ubuntu 24.04), installed libpam-pwquality and configured /etc/security/pwquality.conf with minlen=12 and minclass=3, enabling pam_pwquality.so as a requisite module in /etc/pam.d/common-password via pam-auth-update. Verified enforcement end-to-end by having a real non-root test user change their own password: [REDACTED] (8-char), 12-char/1-class, and 12-char/2-class passwords were all rejected by PAM with explicit policy messages, while a 12-char/3-class password was accepted. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured pre-restart boot_id and policy state, issued a native systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot_id changed after reconnecting, and re-ran the same weak/compliant password test post-restart to confirm the policy persisted and is still enforced, with the system reporting systemctl is-system-running == running.
